tagline: SEO platform built on a proprietary web crawl, keyword, and backlink index.
verdictSummary: A personal rank tracker and on-page auditor for a site you control is a real weekend build. What isn't buildable is the actual product: a backlink index built from a web crawl running continuously for years, plus keyword volume and SERP data at a scale no personal project can match.
coreLoopDIY: A daily rank tracker and a technical SEO crawler for one site you control, backed by a small self-hosted database.
whatYouLose: competitive research on other people's sites
whyPeopleStillPay: Ahrefs sells a dataset, not a dashboard — a web crawl run continuously for years plus licensed keyword and clickstream data. No amount of personal engineering reproduces that alone, in a weekend or ever.
notes: One of the clearest 'no' entries here: state the data moat plainly instead of pretending a crawler script closes the gap.
prompt:
Build a rank tracker and technical SEO auditor for the domains you actually control — not a general SEO platform. For rank tracking: a scheduled job that checks a list of your own keywords against a real SERP API (several have a free tier; do not scrape Google's results pages directly, you'll get blocked quickly) and stores position, ranking URL, and date in a small database, with a simple dashboard showing the trend per keyword. For the audit half: a crawler limited to your own domain that follows internal links and flags the basics — broken links, missing or duplicate titles and descriptions, redirect chains, thin pages — written to a plain report. Pull your real click and impression data for free from the Google Search Console API and show it next to your rank data; budget real time for the OAuth setup, it's the fiddly part. Run this on a schedule with no accounts beyond the API keys it needs.

Do not attempt to build a backlink index, a keyword database, or competitor research on other people's sites — that requires crawling the entire web continuously, which is exactly what you're paying Ahrefs to have already done.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Ahrefs data — my backlink history, my tracked keywords?
faq.a: Your tracked keyword list, yes — that's just a text file you maintain yourself. The backlink index and historical crawl data cannot be exported or rebuilt; that data only exists inside Ahrefs' own crawl.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The dashboard is a small web page, so it renders on a phone browser if you expose it on your network, but there's no dedicated app and no push alerts — you'd have to remember to check it.

faq.q: What does it actually cost to run?
faq.a: A SERP API's free tier usually covers a personal keyword list, and Search Console access is free. Budget a few dollars a month once you outgrow the free tier — a rounding error next to Ahrefs' Starter plan.

faq.q: What's the one thing that genuinely doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Anyone else's site. You can track and audit your own domain all day; you cannot see who links to a competitor or what they rank for — that visibility is the entire product, and it only exists because Ahrefs already crawled it.

faq.q: What's the best free Ahrefs alternative?
faq.a: OpenSEO is the best free Ahrefs alternative for keyword research and tracking on your own sites. It relies on a paid data API for its figures. None of the four projects offers backlink data, so competitor link research stays with Ahrefs.

faq.q: Can a free tool show me my competitors' backlinks?
faq.a: Not with these four projects. None of them has a backlink index or a competitor database. Seonaut and SEOmacroscope crawl your own site, and SerpBear tracks your own rankings. Competitor link data needs a large crawl that a personal project cannot run.

alternativesIntro: The best free Ahrefs alternative is OpenSEO: it handles keyword research and tracking for your own sites. No self-hosted project replaces Ahrefs' backlink index, its keyword volume data or its history of other sites. OpenSEO pulls its numbers from a paid data API (DataForSEO), so it is not free to run at volume. SerpBear is the pick if you only need daily rank tracking for your domain. For a small site you own, these tools are enough. For link research on competitors, keep paying Ahrefs.

alternativeNotes.open-seo: Covers keyword research and tracking, driven by a paid data API. It has no web index of its own and no backlink crawl.
alternativeNotes.serpbear: Tracks keyword rankings daily for your own domain. It has no crawl, no backlink data and no competitor database.
alternativeNotes.seonaut: Crawls a site and lists issues with page reports. It has no rank tracking and no backlink data.
alternativeNotes.seomacroscope: Runs a technical crawl of a site you control. It has no rank tracking and no backlink or keyword database.
